deny.description: Project paths (globs) the assistant never reads, e.g. configs/** holding credentials.

ideas.description: The questions tab offers in an empty chat, by screen (services, logs, ...) or "all"; they come before rig's own.

below.description: Fires when the number drops under the thresholds instead (consumers, ready replicas).

vars.description: The dashboard's $variables, picked in the UI; queries use them as $name.

alerts.description: Add to the project's alerts in this environment.

components.description: components added or replaced here; one without type patches the shared one

description.description: shown by rig env and the TUI

infra.description: the environment that runs this one's shared services; they are started, stopped and reached there, and a Kubernetes runtime gets a Service pointing at the host for each

only.description: services and groups that exist here; dependencies on the rest are dropped

otel.description: fields replacing the project's otel: here (a local environment's endpoints, say)

protected.description: changes need --yes or the TUI's confirmation

queries.description: saved queries replacing the project's of the same name

readonly.description: every change is refused, even with --yes: start, stop, deploy, exec, builds, data and KV writes, load; reads, logs, metrics, traces and read-only queries (SQL in a read-only transaction) still work

runtime.description: a component: type plus the runtime's options (below)

services.description: patches merged into services here: api: { replicas: 3 }

tasks.description: tasks replacing the project's tasks of the same name

fields.description: Fields, when set, are the only other keys shown, in this order; Hide are keys left out (stack, caller, ...) until h shows them.

raw.description: Shows lines as written instead of "LEVEL message key=value"; s switches.

time.description: Time, Level and Message are the JSON keys of those parts, first match wins.

attributes.description: Added to every service's resource, after service.namespace (the project) and deployment.environment (the environment).

endpoint.description: Takes every signal (an OpenTelemetry Collector: svc://otel-collector:4318); Traces, Metrics and Logs send one signal elsewhere, with its full path (svc://jaeger:4318/v1/traces). A signal with no address is off.

sample.description: The fraction of traces kept (parent based); left out, the SDK's default (all).

kind.description: Kind: line (default), stat, gauge, bar (one bar per series, its last value), table.

min.description: And Max bound a gauge (default 0..100 for %, else 0..the largest value).

queries.description: Several queries drawn together (p50, p95 and p99), each with its own legend.

row.description: Starts a new titled row of panels; a panel with only row: is the row's header.

warn.description: And Crit colour stat, gauge and bar values amber and red past them.

width.description: Out of 24 columns, like Grafana (default 12, stat and gauge 6); Height in lines.

path.description: Loads the plugin from a directory instead of the installed store.

version.description: The version or range to use, as rig plugin add writes it.

every.description: Runs the query on a schedule while the UI is open, when Active (or activated there).

ai.description: Adds a summary the assistant writes from the report.

compare.description: Last (or a saved report's time, 20261011-1504): each metric's change against it.

every.description: Adds a timeline: each metric's value per interval of the window.

format.description: Md (default), html, json, xml, csv or junit; a file name's extension wins.

publish.description: Runs these actions with the report: ${report} is its markdown, ${file} its saved file.

schedule.description: Measures and publishes it on a cron schedule (5 fields) while `rig report watch` runs, over the time since its last run.

template.description: Markdown (Go text/template) shown instead of the default layout: {{table "source"}} renders a plugin source, {{.Rows}}, {{.Tests}}, {{.Load}} and {{.Compare}} the measured parts.

tests.description: Adds a suite's last run, Load a load: entry's last result.

verbosity.description: Brief, normal (default) or full: how many series, rows and slow traces it keeps.

build.description: go: ./cmd/api, dockerfile: path (+ context, args), or command: [...]

delay.description: wait this long (10s) after the dependencies are ready before starting the service

depends_on.description: started first; up deploys in phases and waits for each, leaving dependencies that already run untouched

env.description: environment for every runtime; svc://service[:port] inside a value (postgres://app@svc://db:pg/app) becomes the host:port the service reaches in that environment

env_file.description: dotenv files (from the project directory) read under env

extends.description: templates this service starts from, in order

groups.description: names to address several services at once: rig up core

health.description: {port, path}: readiness for local and docker, a readiness probe in generated manifests

image.description: image to run, or the repository name builds push to

manual.description: started only when named or through a group or section, never by all or its role, so rig infra up skips it too (e.g. frontends, an optional Prometheus)

metrics.description: {port, path}: scraped by the scrape metrics adapter

pprof.description: {port, path}: where the pprof profiler connects (default: the metrics port)

replicas.description: left out: keep the running count (or the manifest's); set (0 included) it wins everywhere

role.description: app (default), infra, or load (left out of rig up)

run.description: local runtime: command, args, dir (default: the binary built from build.go)

shared.description: infrastructure one environment runs for others: see environments.<name>.infra

watch.description: {paths, ignore}: what rig watch (ctrl+w in the UI) rebuilds and restarts the service on. Left out: the project packages a build.go main imports, else build.context, else run.dir; .gitignored files, tests and docs never count. Changes settle 0.5s before the rebuild; a failed build keeps the old one running

confirm.description: Asks before the first step, on any environment; --yes answers it.

group.description: The tab the TUI's task picker lists it under; without one, the name's first word (nexus-prune: nexus) when other tasks share it.

readonly.description: Marks a task that changes nothing, so it runs in a read-only environment too.

bench.description: Runs benchmarks matching it (go test -bench); Benchtime and Benchmem tune them.

command.description: Runs the suite through sh instead of go test: pytest, jest, mvn test, cargo test, ... Writing JUnit XML to $RIG_JUNIT gives the screen one row per test; without it the suite passes or fails as a whole by its exit status.

dir.description: Where go test runs (default the project directory).

env.description: Reaches the test binaries; svc:// addresses resolve in the active environment.

exclude.description: Drops packages from Packages (go list patterns: ./pkg/tests/...), so a suite can be "everything but the integration tests".

flags.description: More go test flags; Args go to the test binary after -args.

needs.description: Services (or groups) the suite expects up; the UI warns when they are not.

report.description: A reports: entry measured over each run and saved with it.

runner.description: A plugin's tests/1 runner (pytest, jest, vitest, hurl, k6, junit) instead of go test; With is its options.

lock.description: Keeps people on these pages: no environment picker, command line or mode switch.

mode.description: Detailed (the default), simple (fewer columns, keys and screens), software (the dev screens and views for developers) or product (metrics and views for product); V picks it.

system.description: The system pages kept next to the tabs (SystemPages); left out, all of them.

tabs.description: The screens and views shown, in order (number keys follow it); a name that is not a screen is a view's title. Left out, every screen the project configures something for shows, in the order of Screens.

title.description: Names the UI (its brand and the group of its tabs); left out, the project's name.

slot.description: tab, subtab:<view>, service.section, detail:<scheme>, panel or home; or { tab: { key: K } }

widget.description: a widget kind, when the view is one widget

ignore.description: Globs matched against a changed file's path and name (*_test.go, docs/**).

paths.description: Directories or files (from the project directory); left out, the packages a build.go main imports from the project, else build.context, else run.dir.

agents.description: name: {on, instructions, tools, approve}: assistants that run on an event or a schedule

ai.description: {deny: [globs], instructions: text, ideas: {screen: [questions]}}: project paths the assistant never reads (on top of .env, keys and secrets/), notes it gets with every turn, and the questions tab offers in an empty chat per screen (all for every screen)

alerts.description: thresholds shown in the TUI header and by rig alerts

default.description: environment used when neither -e nor $RIG_ENV is given

defaults.description: section: {keys}: what every entry of that section starts from, below its templates

help.description: Shown by `rig -h` under the project name: this project's own quick-start for its main CLI workflows (e.g. build/deploy/ship with a target database and image tag). Plain text, a few example command lines; left out, `rig -h` shows only its own generic help.

imports.description: services from the files that already define them, read on every load so they stay the only definition: - compose: deploy/compose.yml (image, build, command, ports, env, env_file, depends_on and project volumes, under the compose names; ${VARS} from the environment, then the compose file's .env), - kubernetes: deploy/k8s (a service per Deployment, StatefulSet and DaemonSet, named after it, with its image and container ports; a Kubernetes runtime without manifests: deploys from these folders), - godev: .godev.yaml, - rig: rig.yaml. Each one is a plugin importer (official ones: rig-std install; any plugin can add more); fragments are cached in .rig/cache/import by the files' sha256. A service rig.yaml also defines is the imported one with rig.yaml's keys merged over it (build: null drops an imported key), so rig.yaml holds only what those files have no word for: a Go main to build, health, groups. A workload a rig.yaml service already claims through k8s.workload is not imported again under its own name

include.description: globs of YAML files merged under rig.yaml, later files winning: include: [rig.d/*.yaml]

keys.description: the key preset: rig (the default). A personal choice, so usually in .rig/local.yaml or ~/.config/rig/config.yaml

load.description: named load runs: a generator, a profile, a rate, a duration and assertions for rig load run

manifests.description: folders rig manifests and the Manifests screen read (default: the runtime's manifests, else the kubernetes imports). The screen lists only the objects a service deploys; u shows the rest

otel.description: OpenTelemetry for every app and load service

plugins.description: name: {path, version, off, ...config}: a plugin from path instead of the installed store, a pinned version, off: true to disable it; every other key is the plugin's own config, checked against its schema. Plugins are found in the installed store, ~/.config/rig/plugins/* and, once the workspace is trusted, .rig/plugins/*; the tasks, queries and other rig.yaml keys a plugin carries sit below rig.yaml

policy.description: {roles, bind}: who may run which actions where

project.description: name; also the docker network and container prefix

reports.description: metrics, traces and queries a run is measured by, with tests, load results, compares, templates and publishing: rig report start and stop, rig report, a suite's report:, the Load screen's W

secrets.description: NAME: {help, default}: values kept out of the repo

sections.description: name: {help, services: [names, groups or roles]}: the Services screen's parts, in this order; services in none show under other

tasks.description: name: [shell step, ...] or name: {help, steps}, run in order by rig task <name>

templates.description: partial entries a service, component, task, query, environment, agent or view starts from with extends: name (or a list, applied in order); ${name} in a template is the entry's name

tests.description: test suites for rig test and the Tests screen

ui.description: {tabs, mode, logs, title, system, lock}: the screens and views and their order (a name that is not a screen is a view's title; left out, every screen the project configures something for); title, system and lock make a profile for one audience; mode: detailed (default), simple (fewer screens, columns and keys), software (dev screens and views for developers) or product (metrics and views tagged modes: [product]); V picks one; logs

views.description: name: {slot, title, key, file, <layout or widget>}: a screen built from widgets. slot is tab (default), service.section, panel or home; the body is {widget: table, source: db, query: ..., refresh: 10s, transform: [...]} or a layout (grid: [[a, b], [c]], tabs: {Name: widget}, split, stack, box, scroll); file keeps the body in its own YAML file. See docs/views.md
